reconstructed_theorem_text:
Let E be a finite-dimensional real inner-product space, with its normed additive group structure and its Borel measurable structure; dimension zero is allowed. Let V:E→R be C². Let α,β be nonnegative real numbers with α>0 and α≤β, and assume that, for every x,v∈E,
  α||v||² ≤ (D(DV)(x)[v])[v] ≤ β||v||².
Let η∈R satisfy η>0 and βη≤1.
For arbitrary fixed y,xRef∈E, define c=y−η∇V(xRef). For z=(x,v)∈E×E and t∈R, define
  Φ(t,z)=(c+cos(t)(x−c)+sqrt(η)sin(t)v,
          −sin(t)/sqrt(η)(x−c)+cos(t)v).
Writing d(x)=∇V(x)−∇V(xRef), define
  S(x,v)=(x,v−[2⟨v,d(x)⟩/||d(x)||²]d(x)),
  rate(x,v)=sqrt(η) max(0,⟨v,d(x)⟩),
  Λ(z,t)=∫₀ᵗ rate(Φ(s,z)) ds  for t≥0,
  τ(z,e)=inf{t≥0: Λ(z,t)−e≥0}  for e≥0,
with τ=∞ for an empty hit set. The division in S is total real division, with a/0=0; in particular S leaves z unchanged when d(x)=0. This defines S without a nonzero-gradient-difference premise.
Use the tagged state space RState=([0,∞)×(E×E))⊔{stop}. Define next_e(stop)=stop. For a live record (T,z), set next_e(T,z)=stop when τ(z,e)=∞, and otherwise set next_e(T,z)=(T+τ(z,e), S(Φ(τ(z,e),z))). The infinite case is tested before the finite-value extraction; it is a distinct stop tag, not an infinite timestamp or a zero-time live transition. Given any nonnegative input sequence e, define R₀(e)=(0,z₀) and Rₖ₊₁(e)=next_{eₖ}(Rₖ(e)).
Let Ω=R^N with its coordinate product sigma algebra and let P be the countable product of rate-one exponential laws on R. For every w∈Ω, define ε(w)ₖ=max(wₖ,0), regarded as a nonnegative real. This is a pointwise definition on all real sequences, including sequences with negative coordinates; the measure P is a separate part of the construction. For every fixed natural number n define
  H_n(w)=(R_j(ε(w)))_{0≤j≤n},
  T_n(w)=(w_{n+k})_{k≥0},
  F_n=σ(w↦w_k : k<n).
The history includes the initial record and the record after n successor steps and uses only the clipped versions of coordinates 0 through n−1. The tail is the complete infinite sequence of original real coordinates beginning at n, without clipping.
For every y,xRef,z₀ and every deterministic n∈N, all of the following hold:
(1) H_n and T_n are measurable from the ambient coordinate product sigma algebra to their respective product/tagged Borel target sigma algebras.
(2) For every w,w'∈Ω, if w_k=w'_k for every k<n, then H_n(w)=H_n(w'). This is pointwise equality, without an almost-everywhere restriction.
(3) H_n is measurable when its domain sigma algebra is explicitly chosen to be F_n, the sigma algebra generated by the first n coordinate projections. Its target measurable structure remains the same. This is stronger, distinct information from ambient-domain measurability in (1); it does not choose F_n as the domain sigma algebra for T_n.
(4) (T_n)_*P=P as measures on all real sequences.
(5) H_n and T_n are independent under P, meaning the sigma algebras generated by these random objects are independent. The tail random object in this assertion is the entire infinite tail.
(6) (H_n,T_n)_*P=((H_n)_*P)⊗P as whole measures on the product of the history space and R^N.
(7) For every measurable set A of histories, put B=H_n^{-1}(A). Then
      (T_n)_*(P restricted to B)=P(B)·P
as a whole-measure identity on R^N. The restriction is unnormalized and P(B) is an extended nonnegative scalar. Equivalently, for every measurable C⊆R^N, P(B∩T_n^{-1}(C))=P(B)P(C). If P(B)=0, both measures in the displayed identity are zero, so no positive-probability hypothesis or conditional-probability normalization is required.
All quantification over n is over fixed natural-number depths. There is no assertion here about substituting a random index or arbitrary stopping time for n, about independence of different entries within the history, about finite total event time or absence of explosion, about acceptance/rejection output, about an invariant or target distribution of the phase trajectory, or about a bound on running or query cost. The stated dynamics and assumptions determine the history maps, while the conclusions are the listed measurability, coordinate dependence, product-tail law, independence, joint-law, and restriction-law properties.
objects: E, V, α, β, η; fixed y, xRef, z₀; c, Φ, S, rate, integrated rate Λ, extended crossing time τ; tagged successor next; finite recursive records R; Ω=R^N and product exponential measure P; clipped driving inputs ε; history H_n, full unmodified infinite tail T_n, prefix sigma algebra F_n; history events A and their preimages B.
domains: E is finite-dimensional over R with its inner-product norm and Borel sigma algebra, including dimension zero. α,β∈[0,∞), η∈R. y,xRef∈E; z₀,z∈E×E. Flow times range over R; integrated-rate times and thresholds range over [0,∞). τ has codomain [0,∞] with an explicit infinity value. Records lie in the disjoint union ([0,∞)×(E×E))⊔Unit. Ω consists of every real sequence and has its coordinate product sigma algebra. H_n takes values in RState^{Fin(n+1)} with its inherited finite product/tagged Borel sigma algebra. T_n takes values in Ω. F_n is the join of the comap sigma algebras of coordinate maps k<n, an explicitly chosen domain sigma algebra for H_n. A ranges over measurable subsets of the history target.
quantifiers: Uniformly over every E and structure satisfying the displayed typeclass conditions, every V, α, β, η satisfying the assumptions, then for every fixed y,xRef∈E, every fixed z₀∈E×E, and every deterministic n∈N, the complete conjunction holds. The Hessian inequalities hold for every x,v∈E. Prefix invariance holds for all real sequences w,w′ pointwise. The restriction-law identity holds for every measurable history set A, including events of probability zero. The theorem does not quantify over random indices or random initial conditions.
assumptions: α>0, α≤β with α,β nonnegative; V is twice continuously differentiable; α||v||²≤D²V(x)[v,v]≤β||v||² for every x,v; η>0 and βη≤1. E is a finite-dimensional real inner-product Borel space. P is defined as the countable product of rate-one exponential laws; it is not a freely quantified input law. There are no additional positive-event-probability, nonzero-gradient-difference, non-explosion, nondegenerate-dimension, random-time or target-distribution assumptions.
conclusion: Ambient measurability of H_n and T_n; pointwise dependence of H_n only on raw coordinates k<n; F_n-domain measurability of H_n; exact tail pushforward law (T_n)_*P=P; independence of the history random object and the full infinite tail random object; exact joint pushforward factorization ((H_n)_*P)⊗P; and the unnormalized event-restriction pushforward identity (T_n)_*(P|_{H_n^{-1}(A)})=P(H_n^{-1}(A))·P for every measurable history set A.
scopes: All conclusions are at deterministic finite recursion depth n. H_n includes records 0,…,n, while its last consumed threshold is ε(w)_{n−1}; T_n starts at raw coordinate n and includes all later coordinates. At n=0 the history is constant and the tail is the entire original sequence. Infinite crossing produces an absorbing stop tag; finite crossing advances accumulated time and applies S after Φ. Neither a finite-valued convention at infinity nor a claim of no infinite crossing is made. Coordinate clipping is defined for every real sequence separately from its exponential product law. Ordinary Measurable uses the ambient product domain; Measurable[F_n] explicitly chooses the prefix domain sigma algebra with the same target. Independence concerns these entire maps, not just individual future coordinates. All law equalities are whole-measure equalities. Restriction is not normalized; null events are included. Mathematical source identities and anchors are unavailable.
constant_dependencies: The displayed α,β,η conditions are assumptions, not claimed optimal constants or bounds. c depends on y,xRef,η,V; Φ depends on c,η; S on xRef,V; rate on xRef,η,V; Λ and τ on the same fixed parameters and their displayed state/threshold/time inputs. R and H_n additionally depend on z₀ and the first n thresholds/raw coordinates. T_n and F_n depend only on n. P has the fixed exponential rate 1 and no dependence on y,xRef,z₀,n,V,α,β or η. The restriction scalar is P(H_n^{-1}(A)), so it may depend on A and the history parameters. No asymptotic, dimension-dependent, query-cost, mixing, or hidden positive-probability constants occur in the conclusions.
